note: Window agent p1500-p1599, 1 Nov 2026. events/0: Denmark-Norway was drawn as a vassal of the Duchy of Holstein (inverted vassal_start of Holstein ledger/3, closed in 1526; the effect runs past 1599); events/3: Kerman to the Safavids in summer 1503 (the Aq Qoyunlu 1502 shape now ends in 1502); events/1: Samtskhe land moved from Imereti to the Ottomans after Sokhoista; events/2: whole Abdallab shape as Funj vassal. keyframe_overrides/0-7 give shapes the years their own dossier notes state (Cliopatria rows overlapped the dossier's later keyframes and the compile unions overlapping keyframes). Corrections reach past 1599 only through events/0 (relation closed) and keyframe_overrides/2 (Merv held by Bukhara on 1 January 1600, Safavid gain in 1600 then applies). Orchestrator 3 Nov 2026: dropped events [1] (fx-46: samtskhe-saatabago now regains the land first, so it was a no-op).

events.note: Closes the relation the dossier's ledger/3 opens in the wrong direction, in 1526 when Denmark-Norway is born. The page gives Holstein no overlordship of Denmark or Norway: infobox 'State of the Holy Roman Empire (1474-1806)' and 'Personal union with the Kingdom of Denmark (1474-1544; 1773-1864)'. Because Denmark-Norway is not alive in June 1523 the compile read ledger/3 as Holstein the suzerain and Denmark-Norway (2,934 cells, 1526-1599) the vassal, drawing the whole realm in Holstein's pale vassal tint. Holstein's own 34 cells go to Denmark-Norway's shape in 1526, as in the published draft and in Cliopatria's Denmark.

region.text: the Nile north of the confluence of the Blue and White Niles, with the Butana approximated by River Nile and Khartoum (as the Funj dossier does)

events.note: 1504: 'they were defeated by the Funj Sultanate in 1504 and thereafter ruled over the Butana as vassals' and were 'viceroys of the north and the most important of these vassals'. The dossier's ledger/2 region is Cliopatria's Funj 1507 outline cut to River Nile and Khartoum (275 cells), so only 79 of the Abdallab's cells took the vassal tint; the rest of its shape (River Nile and Khartoum states, 530 cells) was drawn as an independent state beside Funj. This event gives the vassal relation the Abdallab's whole shape.

region.text: the Aq Qoyunlu's Iranian land in the corrected 1502 shape (Iraq-Ajami, Fars, Kerman and the rest of Iran), as aq-qoyunlu ledger/15 gives it to the Safavids in 1503

events.note: Summer 1503: Ismail takes the Aq Qoyunlu's Iranian land. Aq Qoyunlu page: 'He conquered Iraq-Ajami, Fars and Kerman in the summer of 1503'; infobox 'Collapse of the Aq Qoyunlu rule in Iran: Summer 1503'. The Aq Qoyunlu dossier's ledger/15 gives this land (the Iranian part of the corrected 1502 shape) to the Safavids in 1503, but the compile applies that loss only as the Safavid ledger/2 gain (Hamadan, Esfahan, Fars), so with the 1502 shape ended in 1502 (keyframe_overrides/4) the rest (Kerman, 663 cells, and about 1,417 cells of Tehran, Qom, Qazvin, Markazi, Zanjan, Kermanshah, Kurdistan, Khuzestan and the Gulf coast) would fall to nobody until the Safavid 1507 keyframe. [Reviewer, 1 Nov 2026: region widened from Kerman alone to the region of aq-qoyunlu ledger/15; the event takes only cells the Aq Qoyunlu hold, before the Aq Qoyunlu 1503 keyframe snap.]

Aïr, the north-eastern limit of the empire 'from Air in the Northeast to Futa Djallon'
the salt mines of Taghaza 'brought within the empire's boundaries'

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1564 shape plus Dendi, Aïr and Taghaza, for 1564-1590

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's own note says this shape 'holds 1564-1590', but Cliopatria's row runs to 1594, so it overlaps the 1591 Dendi keyframe and keeps the old empire (Agadez, Kayes, Hodh ech Chargui; about 4,100 cells) Songhai until the 1595 keyframe cuts it. Tondibi: 'On 13 March 1591 the armies met'; 'The looting of the three cities marked the end of the Songhai Empire as an effective force'; 'the Songhai themselves moved east to the only surviving province of Dendi'.

union.text: Khorasan: the Iranian province with Mashhad, and Herat

correction.text: the 1588 land with Tashkent and Khorasan (1588: He seized Khorasan), 1588-1597; Merv added in 1593

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's note gives this shape (with Khorasan, Merv added 1593) as 1588-1597, but Cliopatria's row ends in 1594, so from 1595 the Transoxiana-only 1595 shape cut Herat and Khorasan (about 1,740 cells) to nobody three years early. Abdullah Khan II page: 'In 1588 he seized Khorasan'; 'In 1593-94 Khorezm was finally conquered'; 'Abdullah Khan died in 1598'. The Safavid ledger returns Mashhad and Herat only in 1598.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for 1598-1599 only (the Kazakhs hold Samarkand and Fergana after Abdullah Khan II's death), plus the Merv oasis, which Bukhara held from 1593 until the Safavid governor of 1600

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's note says the shape applies 'for 1598-1599 only' but it was compiled from Cliopatria's 1595 row (1595-1599), which cut Herat and Khorasan to nobody three years early. Abdullah Khan II page: 'In 1588 he seized Khorasan'; 'Abdullah Khan died in 1598'. The Merv oasis (294 cells, ledger/14, 1593) is added to the shape because Cliopatria's 1595 outline lacks it and the keyframe would otherwise drop it to nobody in 1598, two years before the Safavids take it. Merv page: 'in 1593, Merv was conquered by Abdullah Khan II of Bukhara'; 'A Safavid governor, Biktash Khan Ustajlu, was appointed to the governorship in 1600'.

region.text: Shanxi, which lies south of the Tumed pastures

rulings.why: Seam sm-04: the same ruling as p1600-p1609 rulings/0, for the years before it. The Tumed dossier draws a 200 km disc round Hohhot that reaches 101-102 cells into Ming Shanxi; the size rule gave them to the smaller Tumed at the conflicts of 1547, 1552, 1582, 1588 and 1595, so the 1599 anchor held 105 Tumed cells in Shanxi. The page puts the Tumed pastures 'north of the border with Shanxi, in present-day Inner Mongolia', and in 1571 Altan 'made peace with the Ming China', so Shanxi stays Ming. The disc's 23 Inner Mongolia and 9 Shaanxi cells are left as drawn (the page does not mention Shaanxi).
